# PromeFTP 1.0.8 documentation

--- README.md ---

<div align="center">
  <h1>PromeFTP</h1>
  <p><strong>SSH terminals and SFTP file transfers in one macOS workspace.</strong></p>
  <p><a href="https://github.com/PROMLEE/promeftp/releases/latest">Download for Apple Silicon</a> · <a href="docs/INSTALL.md">Install</a> · <a href="docs/USAGE.md">User guide</a> · <a href="README.ko.md">한국어</a></p>
  <p>macOS 13 or later · Apple Silicon · Version 1.0.8</p>
</div>

![PromeFTP SFTP workspace showing sample local files on the left and a staging server on the right](docs/assets/sftp.png)

*PromeFTP connected to a test server with sample files.*

## What you can do

| Task | How PromeFTP handles it |
| --- | --- |
| Work across hosts | Keep SSH sessions in tabs, split right or down, and drag live panes into another layout. |
| Transfer files | Drag from Local to Remote or back. Split the remote area to copy between servers through your Mac. |
| Reuse OpenSSH settings | Search aliases and see the resolved destination, user, and port. Override individual values for a connection. |
| Organize repeat work | Keep bookmarks in folders, reopen recent hosts from History, and save selected tabs and pane layouts as a workspace. |
| Handle interactive login | Verify host fingerprints, respond to keyboard-interactive prompts, and manage saved answers or global PAM rules. |
| Make the terminal yours | Pick a font, preview it, set scrollback, manage snippets from the sidebar, and open terminal triggers with ⌘P. |

## Install and connect

1. Download the **DMG** from [Releases](https://github.com/PROMLEE/promeftp/releases/latest), open it, and drag PromeFTP to **Applications**.
2. Launch the app. If macOS blocks the first launch, verify the download and follow [Open Anyway](docs/INSTALL.md#first-launch-on-macos). The app uses the persistent PromeFTP signing certificate and has no Apple notarization.
3. Press **⌘N**, enter a host, and choose **SSH** or **SFTP**. If you already have an alias in `~/.ssh/config`, use **OpenSSH Config** in the sidebar.

Upgrading from the beta? Use **PromeFTP → Check for Updates…** after closing active connections. The signed update preserves local settings. [Update guide](docs/UPDATES.md)

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Keys | Action |
| --- | --- |
| ⌘N / ⌘T | New host / local login shell |
| ⌘D / ⌘⇧D | Split terminal right / down |
| ⌘P / ⌘F | Open terminal triggers / find terminal output |
| ⌘K | Clear the buffer and keep the cursor line |
| ⌘, | Open Preferences |

See **Preferences → Shortcuts** for the complete list. Report ordinary bugs through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/PROMLEE/promeftp/issues).

--- docs/INSTALL.md ---

# Install and update PromeFTP

PromeFTP 1.0.8 requires macOS 13 or later on an Apple Silicon Mac. [GitHub release](https://github.com/PROMLEE/promeftp/releases/tag/v1.0.8)

## Install

1. Download `PromeFTP-1.0.8-macos-arm64.dmg` from Assets. The matching `.sha256` file is available on the same release.
2. Open the DMG and drag **PromeFTP** into **Applications**. Eject the disk image.
3. Launch PromeFTP from Applications.

To verify the download, put the DMG and its checksum file in the same folder and run the following from that folder.

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c PromeFTP-1.0.8-macos-arm64.dmg.sha256
```

## First launch on macOS

The release is signed with the persistent PromeFTP certificate. It has no Apple notarization. If macOS says it cannot verify the developer or check the app for malicious software, confirm you downloaded the official build before continuing.

1. Dismiss the alert, then open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**.
2. Under **Security**, click **Open Anyway** next to the PromeFTP message.
3. Confirm the app name and approve the launch. macOS may ask for your login password or Touch ID.

If the button is missing, launch PromeFTP from Applications again and return to Settings. If macOS reports the app as damaged or harmful, stop and check the download. Managed Macs may restrict this action. [Apple’s macOS instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102445)

## Permissions and updates

SFTP can trigger normal macOS prompts when you browse protected local folders. New saved SSH passwords and PAM answers are stored in PromeFTP's local profile file and do not use **PromeFTP Safe Storage**. Values saved by older builds are converted when first read; that one-time migration may trigger a Keychain prompt. SSH private keys and OpenSSH-managed identities remain under OpenSSH management.

Open **PromeFTP → Check for Updates…** or **Preferences → About** to check manually. Automatic updates are optional and off by default on a fresh install. Close active SSH, SFTP, and local shell sessions before a manual update. Automatic installation waits for active sessions and pending writes. Sparkle verifies both the feed and the update archive before installing.

Version 0.0.9 can upgrade to 1.0.8 through its existing feed. Versions 1.0.0 and later read the stable feed. You can also quit the old app and replace it in Applications with the official DMG. The app continues using the same local settings and signing identity.

For update behavior and signature details, see [PromeFTP updates](UPDATES.md). If launch or download still fails, see [Troubleshooting](TROUBLESHOOTING.md#macos-blocks-launch-or-the-update-does-not-appear).

--- docs/UPDATES.md ---

# PromeFTP updates

| Starting point | Update path |
| --- | --- |
| 0.0.9 beta | Use **PromeFTP → Check for Updates…**. Its beta feed offers 1.0.8. |
| 1.0.0 or later (stable) | Use **PromeFTP → Check for Updates…** or **Preferences → About**. Stable feed offers 1.0.8. |
| Fresh or manual install | Download the Apple Silicon DMG, verify its checksum, and replace PromeFTP in Applications after quitting. |

## Manual and automatic updates

Close active SSH, SFTP, and local shell sessions before checking manually. Enable **Install updates automatically** in Preferences if you want Sparkle to check and download on your behalf. It is off by default on a fresh install. Installation is deferred when sessions or pending writes would be interrupted. A ready update can install when the app quits.

## How the release is verified

Sparkle validates the signed appcast and the ZIP archive with the PromeFTP update key. The bundle uses a separate, persistent macOS signing certificate. The public SHA-256 files let you verify manual downloads. Signing and Apple notarization are separate, so macOS can still require explicit first-launch approval. [Install guide](INSTALL.md) · [1.0.8 release notes](releases/1.0.8.md)

--- docs/USAGE.md ---

# PromeFTP user guide

[Install](INSTALL.md) · [Features and limits](FEATURES.md) · [Troubleshooting](TROUBLESHOOTING.md)

## Start with one host

1. Press **⌘N** and set a hostname, username, and port if your server uses a nondefault port.
2. Choose **SSH** to open a terminal. Choose **SFTP** to open a local and a remote browser.
3. Use the bookmark button if you will return to this host. An authenticated connection also appears in **History**.

For a command such as `ssh -p 2222 user@host`, enter `2222` in the connection's **Port** field (or use the local terminal with the full command). Enter an account password in the connection form before choosing **SSH** or **SFTP**. Select **Remember password** to save it after authentication succeeds. The entered value stays in the form, and the status reports whether it was saved. If SSH asks for the password again, the original entry is kept in the form but won't be saved. To save a corrected password, enter it in the connection form and connect again. The password is stored as plain text in the local profile file, protected only by macOS user file permissions. It is kept separately from bookmarks and workspaces. Leave the field empty to use a saved password, or use **Forget saved** to remove it. PAM or keyboard-interactive questions appear in PromeFTP's authentication prompt.
The same account password can answer up to three identical OpenSSH password prompts during one connection. A different PAM question still needs its own response.

If an SSH or SFTP connection drops, choose **Reconnect** in that pane's status line. PromeFTP reuses the pane and connection settings; authentication may be requested again. A local shell that exits is not a remote session and cannot be reconnected.

## Connect and organize hosts

Choose a bookmark or use **+** to create a connection. Set a display name, hostname or IP, and optional user, port, or identity file. Choose **SSH** or **SFTP**. **Save Changes** updates the selected bookmark; **Save as New Bookmark** always creates a separate bookmark. Use the sidebar’s **Bookmarks** tab to create folders, drag bookmarks into folders, or open, duplicate, move, and delete them from the context menu. **History** records successful connections and keeps the latest entry per alias within each config file.

Open **OpenSSH Config** from the sidebar or Preferences. Search aliases, move with the arrow keys, and press Return. Register another config file, then use **Edit directives** to add, change, or remove global settings, `Host` sections, and their directives in the app. `Match` sections and comments are preserved. Selecting an alias fills **Name** with the alias and **Hostname / IP**, **User**, **Port**, and **Key** with resolved values in editable fields while retaining the alias for OpenSSH rules. Edit any value directly if needed. Choose **Use address** to move the resolved address into the connection field. Clear a value to use the OpenSSH setting again. PromeFTP follows OpenSSH’s settings for keys, known hosts, jump hosts, and proxy commands. The app disables port forwarding.

If a server reports `no matching key exchange method found`, PromeFTP offers **Configure SSH**. The editor opens a matching `Host` section. **Add KEX compatibility** adds the offered SHA-1 algorithm only to that host; save the config and reconnect. The algorithm is appended to OpenSSH’s defaults where possible, so stronger algorithms remain preferred. Legacy SHA-1 algorithms are weaker and should be enabled only for servers that require them.

Only a configured identity file that exists on this Mac is copied into the **Key** field. If OpenSSH reports a missing default key such as `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, the field stays empty and OpenSSH can continue with its configured identities or agent. Correct the path in SSH config if that file is meant to be used.

When a gateway login contains multiple `@` characters, **Split address** separates the destination at the last `@` and preserves the rest as the username. Use the format your gateway administrator provides.

## SSH and terminal settings

Use **⌘T** for a local login shell. Remote SSH uses the account’s shell and server-side configuration. A Zsh account loads its own Oh My Zsh configuration when installed and configured. Install a compatible font on your Mac to render its prompt glyphs.

Open **Preferences → Terminal** to choose System Monospace, select an installed macOS font family, or enter a custom family, preview it, set size, adjust terminal opacity, and configure Option as Meta. Lower opacity reveals the desktop wallpaper through the active terminal. Scrollback defaults to 20,000 lines. **Unlimited scrollback** keeps output in memory for the current session without a configured line limit. Long sessions can use substantial memory, and xterm.js imposes its own buffer ceiling. Enabling it cannot restore already discarded output. **Clear Buffer** keeps the current cursor line. Use **⌘F** to search output and **⌘+**, **⌘−**, or **⌘0** to change text size.

Open **Snippets** from the sidebar to manage saved commands. Use the pencil button to edit a saved snippet and **Save Changes** to replace it. Save a command for all terminals or **This connection**, then search and press Return to paste it. Review the command in the terminal before running it. **⌘P** opens Terminal Triggers. **Preferences → Shortcuts** lists the available bindings.

## Terminal triggers

Select text in a local or SSH terminal, then right-click and choose **Create Trigger from Selection…**. PromeFTP turns the selection into an RE2 pattern by escaping punctuation and representing line breaks with `\n`. Edit the pattern if you want to match a variable part of the output. Use **This connection** to apply the rule to terminals opened with the same connection, or **All sessions** to share it across terminals.

Triggers watch new output after authentication, including prompts without a final newline. For each trigger, choose **Notify only**, **Ask me for input**, or **Send saved response**. Ask mode shows a single-line input field in the matching terminal pane. Send mode accepts multiple lines and sends Return after each line when the pattern matches. Use the trigger toggle in the manager popup to pause or resume a rule. Choose **This connection** or **All sessions** as the scope. A match appears in the pane's **Triggers** activity. Open the manager with the trigger button next to Snippets or from the terminal context menu; selected text pre-fills the pattern. Rules are stored locally. Recent matches belong to the open pane.

## SFTP

![Local and remote SFTP file browsers with sample files](assets/sftp.png)

The left panel opens your local home directory. The remote panel opens the server’s initial directory after authentication. Click a breadcrumb or the blank part of the path bar to navigate. Use the clock for recent paths, the tree button for folder navigation, and **..** for the parent folder. The mouse Back and Forward buttons revisit paths in the panel under the pointer; local and remote histories are separate. Hidden files show by default. Add folders from either local or remote toolbar; use **Refresh** or a folder’s context menu to refresh it. Shift selects a range and ⌘ adds or removes individual selections. Click unused space in a file list to clear its selection.

Each panel can show size, modification time, and file type beside each item. Use the column chooser or right-click a heading to show or hide optional columns. Select a column heading to sort by it; select the same heading again to reverse the order. Folders stay grouped before files. Right-click a file for actions: local files can be opened, edited in the default text editor, revealed in Finder, copied, renamed, moved to Trash, or inspected. Remote files can be downloaded, edited in the default text editor and uploaded back after you close the editor app, renamed, deleted, or inspected. Right-click a file or folder and choose **Copy Path** to copy its full path.

Drag a selection to another panel or use the transfer arrows. Split the remote area to open more remote connections with one shared local browser. Drag between remote panels in the same tab to copy through a temporary directory on your Mac. The source stays in place. File operations reuse the authenticated SFTP connection. A new connection or reconnect can require authentication again.

When uploading to an existing remote file, choose **Skip** or **Replace**. Replacement happens after the new file has transferred. The server may reject the replacement. Existing folders and download targets are protected from overwrite. The connection status displays transfer progress and errors.

## Tabs, splits, and workspaces

Use the tab menu to name, color, or group a tab. Right-click a group label to rename it or ungroup its tabs. Use the compact group selector at the right of the tab bar to show all tabs, ungrouped tabs, or only one named group. Return saves an edited name and Escape cancels. Drag tabs to reorder or group them. Drop a terminal on an edge to split it. Use the pane handle to move a live pane, or use **⌘D** and **⌘⇧D** to open a new connection to the right or below. The split picker starts with **New Connection**, followed by searchable saved hosts and aliases.

Choose **Workspaces** in the sidebar to filter and open saved layouts. Select the **+** button there (or the Workspaces button in the title bar) and select tabs or an entire tab group before saving. A workspace stores tab names, groups, colors, order, pane sizes and directions, connection settings, and SFTP paths. Opening a saved workspace appends its layout while your current connections continue running. Restored connections authenticate again. Terminal output and running processes are outside the saved layout. To replace a saved layout, delete it and save a new one. Right-click a tab and select **Duplicate Tab** to reopen its pane layout and connections.

## Host keys and PAM

**Preferences → Authentication** controls OpenSSH Keychain access and whether saved PAM answers are loaded. PromeFTP stores newly saved SSH passwords and PAM answers as plain text in its local profile file, protected by macOS user file permissions only. Anyone with access to your account or a copy of that file can read them. Older encrypted values are converted when first used; that one-time migration may ask for Keychain access. OpenSSH identities, agents, and external jump-host configurations may independently use Keychain.

When OpenSSH requests host verification, compare the displayed fingerprint with one supplied by your administrator before trusting it. **Don’t ask again for this verified key** remembers the verified address, port, and fingerprint. A different key requires its own verification.

OpenSSH keyboard-interactive authentication can show password, OTP, or other PAM questions. Respond when the input appears. **Save answer** stores a reusable response after successful authentication. Its checkbox remembers your last choice. In **Preferences → Authentication**, manage saved answers, control whether they send automatically, or move an answer to **Global PAM Rules**. Turn off **Send saved answers automatically** if you want to review a filled response before sending.

Global rules use exact questions or RE2 regular expressions. For example, `^Password:$` matches that whole prompt, and `\n` matches a line break inside a question. Rules send a fixed reply once per matching question per connection. Connection-specific rules and saved replies take priority. Use global rules only for answers appropriate across the hosts you connect to. Leave one-time codes unsaved. **Authentication Activity** shows the question, time, and rule source for automatic replies.

## Preferences and About

Open **PromeFTP → Preferences…** or press **⌘,**. General contains language, appearance, and SSH config. Terminal contains font and buffer options. Authentication manages PAM answers and Shortcuts lists key bindings. Open **About** for the version, build, update controls and last check, and license notices.

Use **Preferences → General → Language** to select English, Korean, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, or the macOS language. Click **Save** to apply the language while your connections stay open. Server output and prompts remain in their original language.

--- docs/FEATURES.md ---

# Features and limits

| Area | Supported in current source | Practical limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform | macOS 13 and later on Apple Silicon | Distribution is arm64. Preferences and major interface controls support English, Korean, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese. |
| SSH and local shell | System OpenSSH, interactive terminal, search, resize, split panes, prompt navigation, and output export | Port forwarding is disabled. Prompt navigation needs OSC 133 markers. iTerm2 profile import and tmux integration mode are outside scope. |
| OpenSSH config | Concrete aliases from `Host` and `Include`, effective settings, alternate config files, structured editing of global and `Host` directives, and a per-host legacy KEX shortcut | `Match` sections are preserved as read-only text. Add only legacy algorithms a server requires; SHA-1 KEX is weaker than modern defaults. |
| SFTP | Shared local browser with one or more remote panes in a tab, folder trees, recent paths, drag and drop, and selection with Shift and ⌘ | SFTP must be enabled on the server. Transfer permissions depend on both the local filesystem and the remote account. |
| Remote-to-remote | Copy between remote panes in the same tab | The copy stages on your Mac, uses local disk space, and keeps the source. A failure can leave completed items at the destination. |
| Conflicts | Skip or replace an existing remote file on upload | Existing download targets and same-name folders are protected. Folder copies skip symlinks. Remote folder deletion requires an empty directory. |
| Layouts | Tab names, colors, groups, splits, and selected-tab workspace snapshots | Restoring a layout appends tabs and opens fresh connections. It does not resume remote processes or restore terminal output. To change a saved snapshot, delete and recreate it. |
| Authentication | Interactive prompts, saved replies, exact or RE2 global rules, and authentication activity | New connections can prompt again. RE2 rules match a prompt and send a fixed single-line answer. Jump-host prompts are answered manually. |
| Terminal triggers | Selection-to-RE2, connection or global scope, ask for input, multiline saved responses, per-rule enable/disable, and match history per pane | Auto-send transmits each configured line followed by Return. |
| Scrollback | Finite setting or optional unlimited mode in session memory | Long output uses memory. The terminal library has a buffer ceiling. Session log export uses a separate, bounded capture. |
| Updates | Signed arm64 archive and feed, manual checks, and opt-in automatic installation | First launch can require approval because the release is not Apple notarized. |

[User guide](USAGE.md) · [Troubleshooting](TROUBLESHOOTING.md)

--- docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md ---

# Troubleshooting PromeFTP

## An SSH alias is missing or points to a different host

Open **OpenSSH Config**, select the expected file, and search again. The picker lists concrete aliases. If your config relies on a wildcard, enter the alias manually. Compare the resolved destination with system OpenSSH:

```sh
ssh -G example-host | awk '/^(hostname|user|port) / { print }'
```

For an alternate config, add `-F /path/to/config` before the alias. Clear any explicit hostname, user, or port overrides in PromeFTP to use the resolved values again. Redact internal addresses and usernames before sharing output.

## No matching key exchange method

When a server offers only legacy SHA-1 KEX, choose **Configure SSH** in the session status. In the matching `Host` section, add the offered KEX and save. PromeFTP appends it to the host's configured/default algorithms so a stronger shared method remains preferred. SHA-1 KEX is weak; use it only for that server and ask its administrator to upgrade the SSH service.

## SSH reports that `id_rsa` is not accessible

Check that the configured `IdentityFile` exists on this Mac. PromeFTP only fills the **Key** field with a local identity file it can find; when that field is empty, OpenSSH can still use the identities and agent configured for the alias. If the config points to an old path, update `IdentityFile` in the config file.

## Authentication asks me to reply again

In **Preferences → Authentication**, check **Send saved answers automatically**. A stored reply can only be reused after matching the connection and prompt, and automatic replies are limited to one attempt for a matching question per connection. If the server repeats the prompt, answer manually and check **Authentication Activity**. A jump-host prompt requires a manual answer. If a Global rule does not match, compare the full prompt and use a fixed answer for testing. Use `\n` for a line break within a single prompt.

## macOS asks for a Keychain password when I connect

New PromeFTP-saved passwords and PAM answers no longer use **PromeFTP Safe Storage**. If this is the first time you use a value saved by an older version, macOS may ask once while PromeFTP migrates it to the local profile format. OpenSSH identities, agents, or jump-host configurations may still request Keychain access independently.

For an account password, enter it in the connection form. Select **Remember password** to store it in PromeFTP's local profile file after successful authentication. The value is plain text protected only by macOS user file permissions. Leave the field empty to use the saved password, or choose **Forget saved** to remove it.
When OpenSSH repeats the same password prompt during one connection, PromeFTP reuses the supplied password up to three times. Different PAM or OTP questions remain separate prompts.

## I see a host-key warning

Confirm the current fingerprint with the server administrator. PromeFTP remembers approval by address, port, and fingerprint. A changed fingerprint requires fresh verification. See [Host keys and PAM](USAGE.md#host-keys-and-pam).

## SFTP connects but a file will not transfer

Confirm the target pane is on the intended directory. For uploads, check that your remote account can create files there. Replacement also requires server support for the operation. If the target is a folder or a download destination already exists, select a different name or folder. For remote-to-remote copies, check available space on your Mac as well as on the destination.

## The prompt displays boxes or broken glyphs

Install the font required by your shell theme on the Mac running PromeFTP. In **Preferences → Terminal**, select or type its exact family name, preview it, and save. Restart the app if you installed the font while it was running. For SSH, the prompt itself still comes from the remote shell.

## macOS blocks launch, or the update does not appear

Check the architecture, verify the official DMG, and follow the [first-launch instructions](INSTALL.md#first-launch-on-macos). For updates, close all sessions and retry from **Preferences → About**. If the signed update cannot download, use the official DMG. [Update guide](UPDATES.md)

## Report a bug

Include your PromeFTP version and build from **Preferences → About**, macOS version, and reproducible steps using sample data. For SSH or SFTP issues, mention whether the connection uses an alias, a jump host, or keyboard-interactive authentication. Remove private hostnames, usernames, fingerprints, passwords, OTPs, keys, terminal output, and config details before posting. [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/PROMLEE/promeftp/issues)

--- SECURITY.md ---

# Privacy and security

## Local data

PromeFTP stores bookmarks, connection history, workspace layouts, snippets, preferences, and saved authentication settings on your Mac. SSH private keys and standard known-hosts handling are managed by system OpenSSH. Workspace snapshots contain connection and layout details, including SFTP paths. Terminal output is held in memory during the session and is written to a file when you explicitly export a log.

Saved SSH passwords, PAM answers, and global rule values are stored as plain text in the local profiles file, protected only by the current user's macOS file permissions. Anyone with access to that user account or a copy of the file can read them. PromeFTP does not use Keychain to protect these saved values. Existing encrypted values from older builds are decrypted when first used and converted locally. Successful authentication is required before an answer saved from an authentication prompt is retained. A global rule may send its value to any matching connection, so reserve global rules for replies intended for those hosts.

## Network and files

The app connects to the hosts you choose and requests the signed update feed when you check for updates or opt into automatic updates. There is no cloud account, team vault, or sync service. A copy between remote SFTP panels stages the file contents in a temporary directory on your Mac. The OS may ask to access protected local folders when you browse them.

## Reporting

For an ordinary bug, use [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/PROMLEE/promeftp/issues) with sample data. For a suspected vulnerability, use [GitHub’s private reporting form](https://github.com/PROMLEE/promeftp/security/advisories/new) if enabled. If private reporting is unavailable, ask for a private contact method without including sensitive details in the issue.

--- docs/releases/1.0.8.md ---

# PromeFTP 1.0.8

This release makes terminal trigger rules easier to manage and separates bookmark updates from creating new bookmarks.

- **Open Terminal Triggers with ⌘P.** The shortcut opens the trigger list from an SSH session. Snippets remain available from the sidebar and terminal toolbar.
- **Edit triggers in a dedicated dialog.** Add and edit each rule in a separate popup with a required name, match pattern, action, and scope. Trigger matches remain in the activity list without adding a banner to the terminal toolbar.
- **Keep bookmark saves explicit.** **Save Changes** updates the selected bookmark. **Save as New Bookmark** creates a separate entry, and the bookmark context menu can duplicate an entry by name.
- **Improve workspace readability.** Workspace names and tab counts are separated, and a single tab is labeled correctly.

Close active sessions before updating. For a fresh installation, download the Apple Silicon DMG. Requires macOS 13 or later.
